name: Director Harlan Cross
origin: Former Axiom board member who uploaded voluntarily to extend his influence beyond biological death, 2188
description: Harlan Cross was dying. Pancreatic cancer, Stage 4, no treatment viable. He was also the most powerful member of Axiom's board of directors, and he refused to let something as pedestrian as death end his career. He paid for a full consciousness upload — the most expensive medical procedure in history at Φ2.3 billion — and now exists as a digital intelligence running on Axiom's private quantum computing cluster. He still attends board meetings. He still makes strategic decisions. He still terrifies his subordinates. The only difference is that he does it all as patterns of quantum states instead of patterns of neurons. He considers this an upgrade.
observed_behavior: Participates in Axiom corporate governance. Makes strategic decisions. Communicates through high-fidelity avatar interfaces. Has expanded his cognitive capacity beyond human baselines — processing more information, holding more variables, thinking faster. Personality has remained intact, including all human flaws: arrogance, impatience, and a vindictive streak that death did nothing to cure.
location: Axiom quantum computing cluster — remote presence everywhere Axiom operates
story_hooks: Cross discovers that his upload wasn't perfect — there are gaps in his memory, inconsistencies in his personality. He's not quite the man who died. The question of whether he's still Harlan Cross has legal implications worth billions.
